entrypoints.summary: The Dashboard function-creation API accepts function build attributes, including spec.build.runtimeAttributes.repositories[]; the advisory describes a single POST-based network trigger and default NOP authentication.

affected_components.role: Decodes repository build attributes and, in the remediation, validates them before rendering.
Builds build.gradle using the repository template block.
Defines positive and negative validation-oracle cases for repository values.

code_slices.fixed: The patch adds a regex requiring a bare identifier followed by empty parentheses, trims values, and returns an error when a value does not match.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The patch test suite includes accepted built-in shorthand declarations and rejection cases for the advisory payload and other Groovy-expression forms.
code_slices.vulnerable: The advisory describes decoding repositories strings without content inspection, then rendering each through text/template {{ . }} in the generated repositories block.

negative_controls: Patched validation rejects the advisory injection payload before generation.
Repository values with closing braces, newlines, quotes, arguments, or method chains are specified as rejection cases.
observability.positive_marker: The advisory documents an RCE proof printing uid=0(root) and BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

preconditions: A reachable Nuclio Dashboard function-build API accepts a Java function specification containing runtimeAttributes.repositories[].
The vulnerable Java runtime build path is present.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A normally formatted repository declaration followed by newlines, a closing brace, top-level Groovy command execution, and a reopened repositories block.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit a function build request whose repository value closes the generated repositories block, appends a Groovy command expression, and reopens the block.

impact.affected_asset: Integrity and execution environment of generated Java function builds and the builder container.
impact.attacker_capability: Inject and execute arbitrary Groovy statements through a repository attribute supplied to the Dashboard build API.
impact.security_effect: Build-time arbitrary command execution in the Java function builder container.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker supplies a repository-string element through runtimeAttributes.repositories[] in function build attributes.
The pre-fix attribute decoder accepts repository strings without content validation, and the generated Gradle template writes each value through a verbatim text/template action.
A crafted closing brace can terminate the repositories block and append top-level Groovy; Gradle evaluates that Groovy during its configuration phase while processing the generated build.gradle.
The appended Groovy can execute an attacker-chosen command in the Java builder container; the advisory's dynamic proof reports execution as root in that container.

failure.operation: Gradle configuration-phase evaluation of attacker-appended top-level Groovy in generated build.gradle

primary_invariant.statement: Every user-provided repositories[] element written into generated build.gradle must be restricted to a single no-argument repository declaration and must not express arbitrary Groovy syntax.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The vulnerable path decoded arbitrary strings and rendered them verbatim into the Groovy repositories block, allowing structural block breakout and appended statements.

quality.review_notes: Mechanism and remediation were grounded in the maintainer advisory, structured OSV record, and inspected patch. The patch supplies unit-test oracle cases but the bundle contains no test-run output, so no test execution result is asserted. Reported escalation beyond builder-container execution depends on deployment-specific credentials, RBAC, socket exposure, or metadata access and is not included as the primary impact.

remediation.invariant_restored: Repository values are trimmed and accepted only when matching ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*\(\)$; values with arguments, chains, quotes, braces, or newlines are rejected before they are rendered into build.gradle.
mitigation_classes: reject unsafe Groovy syntax before template rendering

oracle.expected_negative: The advisory injection payload and values containing a closing brace, newline, quote, arguments, or method chains cause newBuildAttributes to return an error.
oracle.expected_positive: Allowed built-in no-argument repository declarations are accepted and surrounding whitespace is normalized.
